# My plan for this year

Alright, let me think through this season. I've been on this land 45 years now, and at my age you learn to be careful but not stubborn — the wheat harvests I got best were when I paid attention to what the soil was telling me, not when I just did what my father did.

## How I'm splitting the 10.1 mu

I run the wheat-maize double crop on 6 mu — the better fields closer to the well, because that rotation needs water at the right moments. The other 4.1 mu I keep in cotton. Cotton pays better per mu when the market holds up, but it's backbreaking work, and with just my wife and me in the house now (the kids are working in the city), I can't put everything in cotton. Picking it alone would kill us. Four mu is about what the two of us can manage with maybe a week of hired help at peak picking.

## Wheat (already in the ground, planted last October)

I put my wheat down around October 10th last fall. Looking at it now in late April, it's heading out. I used a good seminal improved variety — Jimai 22 — cost me about 35 yuan per mu for certified seed but I don't save my own seed anymore, the yield drop-off isn't worth it.

Before sowing I spread 40 kg of compound fertilizer per mu (15-15-15), which gives me roughly 6 kg N base, 6 kg P₂O₅, and 6 kg K₂O. Then I topdressed 25 kg urea per mu at jointing in late March — that's another 11 kg N. So my total N works out to about 17 kg/mu, which is what I've found works for a realistic 450 kg/mu target on my soil. I know the extension station talks about 20+ but on my fields anything above 18 just ends up lodging in wet years.

Irrigation: I've already done winter watering in December and the jointing water in late March. I'll do one more at heading-filling around May 10-15 if we don't get decent rain, and probably skip the fourth. Each irrigation costs me about 25 yuan per mu in electricity and my time at the pump — not nothing on 6 mu.

I'll spray herbicide (tribenuron-methyl) once, already done that in early April for the broadleaf weeds. One fungicide spray at heading if I see stripe rust starting — the neighbors' fields will tell me.

**Yield expectation: 450 kg/mu** — that's what I got the last three years average. If we get good May rain it could touch 500.

## Maize (planting mid-June right after wheat)

Tight turnaround — I've got maybe 5 days between combine-harvesting wheat and sowing maize. I'll use no-till direct drilling with the hired machine (the village cooperative operator, 40 yuan/mu). Zhengdan 958 or a similar hybrid, about 50 yuan/mu for seed.

For maize I'll put down 35 kg of compound fertilizer (15-15-15) at sowing — that's my starter — and then topdress 20 kg urea at the big trumpet stage in late July. Total N around 15 kg/mu. Maize responds well but cost per kg of yield isn't as good as people think when fertilizer prices are up like now.

Irrigation usually once at tasseling if July is dry. Often we get enough rain in July-August and I skip it entirely. That's one advantage of summer maize on the plain.

Herbicide at sowing (atrazine + acetochlor mix). Usually one spray against corn borer if I see eggs.

**Yield expectation: 500 kg/mu** — the wheat-maize rotation gives a good N carryover for the maize, which is part of why I stick with it.

## Cotton (planting now, late April)

This is the decision that keeps me up at night. Cotton prices have been up and down, labor for picking is getting impossible to find, and at 63 I can't bend over a cotton row for 10 hours like I used to. But cotton is what grew here when I was young, the fields on that side of the village aren't as good for the wheat-maize rotation (sandier soil), and the gross return per mu is still the best I can get.

Planting now, end of April when the soil temperature is finally steady above 15°C. I'm using a Bt hybrid variety — about 50 yuan/mu for seed, but the bollworm protection is worth it because I spray much less than I used to. Film-covered ridges, planted with the hand-pushed seeder.

Fertilizer: 50 kg compound (15-15-15) before ridging, plus 15 kg urea at flowering in July. Total N around 14 kg/mu. I put more potassium on cotton than on grain — cotton really wants K for fiber quality. I'll add 10 kg of potassium sulfate per mu.

Irrigation twice — once at first flower in late June, once at peak boll-setting in early August. Cotton doesn't like wet feet but it really needs water at those two points.

Pesticide: I'll probably do 3-4 sprays over the season — mainly for aphids early and mirids mid-season. Not bollworm thanks to the Bt.

**Yield expectation: 270 kg/mu** of lint cotton.

## What I'm worried about this year

Fertilizer prices are still high compared to five years ago, so I'm being a bit tighter on rates than I'd like. If wheat prices hold at 2.6 yuan/kg I'll be fine. If cotton drops below 6 yuan/kg seed cotton I'll lose money on the cotton fields and next year I might convert those 4 mu to wheat-maize too. But I'm not making that decision this year — the cotton is going in the ground this week.

Water is another worry. The water table has kept dropping. My neighbor's well needed deepening last year, 3000 yuan. Mine is fine for now but I can't keep pulling the same volumes forever.
